alt: AI illustration: an open sketchbook with pencils and crayons on a table by a window, where a house crow looks in.
prompt: A wooden table top in front of an open window with turquoise-painted wooden shutters and a flat iron grill. On the table lies an open sketchbook with clean cream pages, blank except for one faint pencil circle and two light curved guide lines. Beside it are two sharpened pencils, an eraser and a small open box of wax crayons in marigold, terracotta, turquoise and leaf green, all tidy in their box. Just outside the window, a house crow perches on the grill's bottom bar and peers in at the sketchbook, head tilted, curious. A compact, self-contained vignette: window and table form one simple shape, and the crow reads clearly at about 300 px.
whyChosen: Kindness chain, step 1: sitting down to draw an animal you have watched.

title: A kinder street corner
alt: AI illustration: a quiet street corner where a dog rests in the shade near a bowl of clean water, and a cat sits on the wall above.
prompt: A calm corner of a residential street. A leafy neem tree grows beside a home's low garden wall of cream lime plaster with a terracotta-red coping and an open, green-painted gate. In the tree's shade, just inside the open gate, sits a wide, heavy terracotta bowl of clean water with one small stone in it. The fawn Indie dog lies resting in the shade a few steps from the bowl: head up, eyes soft, mouth closed, relaxed. The orange-and-white street cat sits on top of the wall with its tail curled around its paws, eyes half-closed in a slow blink. A few fallen neem leaves lie on the ground. A compact, self-contained vignette: tree, wall and animals form one simple shape that reads at about 300 px.
whyChosen: Kindness chain, step 3: a kinder street, with shade, clean water and calm animals.

title: A school notice board, waiting for pictures
alt: AI illustration: a school notice board with blank sheets of coloured paper pinned up, waiting for pictures, and a pigeon watching from the window sill.
prompt: A short stretch of a school corridor wall in cream lime plaster with a terracotta-red band along its base. On it hangs a cork notice board in a simple wooden frame, seen from a few steps away. Pinned to it with round coloured pins are three white-bordered instant-photo prints of street animals drawn in the same style — a fawn Indie dog sitting, an orange-and-white cat, a house crow on a wall — and two plain coloured cards (marigold and turquoise). To the right is an open corridor window with a stone sill, where a rock pigeon stands and looks across at the photos with interest. Board and window form one simple shape; the pigeon reads clearly at about 300 px. The Indian house crow has a glossy black forehead, crown, face, throat and bill, and a soft ash-grey collar only on its nape, neck and upper breast; black wings and tail. (Then the pinned dog photo redrawn as a lean Indie with upright ears, and the crow's grey kept to its neck and breast.) (Last, by script and not by AI, the three pinned prints were painted over as blank sheets of pale coloured paper, so no made-up picture stands in for a child’s work.)
whyChosen: Kindness chain, step 2: a wall waiting for children’s work, so others notice the animals too.

title: Ankle bells, a scroll and three friends
alt: AI illustration: a dancer’s brass ankle bells and a rolled scroll tied with ribbon rest on a veranda, watched by a myna, a calm dog and a resting cow.
prompt: A calm symbolic still life on the shaded front veranda of an old South Indian house, seen at low eye level in morning light. At the centre, on a low wooden plank seat, lies a rolled cream scroll tied with a terracotta-red ribbon in a neat bow. Coiled at rest beside it on the plank is a pair of dancer's ankle bells: rows of small round brass bells sewn onto red padded straps with long cotton ties, unworn and glinting. A few jasmine buds and marigold heads lie scattered around them. A common myna (brown body, glossy black head, yellow eye-patch and bill) perches on the end of the scroll, head tilted toward the bells. On the cool red-oxide floor just right of the plank, the fawn Indie dog (white chest blaze, upright ears) lies relaxed with its head on its paws, watching the bells. Just beyond the low veranda step, in the sunlit courtyard behind, the cream zebu cow lies resting and chewing, her small brass bell echoing the dancer's bells. A white rice-flour kolam loops across the floor in the foreground, and a carved wooden pillar stands at the far right edge. Keep the scroll, the bells, the myna, the dog's head and the cow's head within the middle half of the width, because one card crops this image close to square or slightly tall. (Then re-rendered as flat gouache with hand-inked outlines, in even focus.)
whyChosen: Story cover: a still life for the dancer who asked Parliament to protect animals.

title: A greater adjutant stork’s nest
alt: AI illustration: a giant greater adjutant stork shelters two fluffy chicks in a stick nest high in a flowering tree, while its mate glides in over a quiet village garden.
prompt: Wide village scene viewed from a respectful distance on a fresh early morning. A tall silk-cotton tree rises from a homestead garden just right of centre, its high branches dotted with scarlet blossoms and new leaves. In its topmost fork, about 60% across and a quarter down from the top, sits a broad, sturdy nest of sticks. On the nest rim stands a greater adjutant stork: very tall, slate-grey wings and back, white underparts and a fluffy white neck ruff, bare pink-orange head and neck, a massive pale-yellow wedge-shaped bill, a pink-orange throat pouch and long pale legs. It holds one wing half-open like a sheltering umbrella over two fluffy grey chicks whose round heads peek up beside it, safe and content. Left of centre in the sky, its mate glides in toward the nest on huge outspread wings, neck tucked back and legs trailing, showing how enormous the bird is. Below lies the garden: areca-nut palms and banana plants, a low bamboo fence ringing the foot of the tree, a marigold garland tied around the trunk like a welcome, and a handwoven cream cloth with a red border woven with a row of tiny stork shapes, drying on a bamboo pole. At the far left, part of a raised village house with a sloping turquoise tin roof. Keep the nest, both storks and the garland within the central 85% of the width so a 4:3 centre crop keeps them.
whyChosen: Story cover: the village that throws a baby shower for the hargila stork.

title: Street cat waking up
prompt: Start: The orange-and-white street cat from the model sheet, asleep in a neat loaf on the flat top of a short wall segment. Its body is tucked into a rounded bread-loaf shape, front paws folded out of sight under its chest, tail lying along its side, eyes closed in calm crescents, chin slightly lowered, ears relaxed. The wall segment is a short, level slab of cream lime plaster with a terracotta-red coping band along its perfectly flat top, with its front face visible. It spans the middle 70% of the frame width; its top edge is at about 68% of the frame height and its bottom edge at about 85%. The cat is centred on the wall, in a three-quarter front view at the cat's eye level. Scale the cat so that when it later sits upright on this spot, its ear tips reach about 15 to 20% from the top of the frame. At least 15% empty margin on every side; nothing else in the frame. End: Edit of the start keyframe. Keep the same cat, markings, wall slab, camera angle, framing, scale and colours exactly, and change only the cat's pose. The cat is now awake and sitting upright on the same spot on the wall top: front legs straight and together, tail curled neatly around its front paws, ears up, whiskers relaxed. Its amber eyes are half-closed in a slow, content blink, gazing toward the viewer. Ear tips about 15 to 20% below the top edge; at least 15% empty margin on every side; nothing else in the frame. Motion: Locked camera: the loafing cat opens its eyes, reaches its front paws forward in one long, low, comfortable stretch along the wall top, then sits up on the same spot, curls its tail around its paws and gives one slow, content blink toward the viewer, while the wall stays perfectly still.
whyChosen: Footer of every page: the cat wakes and gives the slow blink, a cat’s friendly hello.

title: Indie dog waking up
prompt: Start: A lean, healthy fawn Indian pariah dog (an Indie): a short, smooth coat, a slim body, a long narrow muzzle, large upright pointed ears, a white chest blaze and white paw tips, and a thin, sickle-curved tail. Never fluffy, never a Shiba Inu, a Spitz or a fox. It naps on a warm day in a loose, relaxed crescent on its chest and side, chin resting on its crossed front paws, eyes closed in calm crescents, one ear half-raised as if listening. Its thin tail lies softly along its flank, away from its face. One dog only, seen from a low three-quarter front view at its eye level, centred, on a flat chroma-green background. Warm brown-black hand-inked outlines, flat gouache fills with subtle grain; no collar, no text, no people. End: Edit of the start keyframe: the same dog, markings, framing and ground line; now awake and lying on its chest on the spot where it slept, in a relaxed sphinx pose, front legs stretched forward, head raised and turned toward the viewer with a small, curious tilt, mouth gently closed in a soft smile, calm warm-brown eyes. Motion: Locked-off static shot. The napping Indie dog wakes in its own time: one ear pricks up and then the other, it stretches its front legs forward along the ground, lifts its head from its paws and settles on its chest, ending with a small, curious head tilt as it calmly watches the viewer. It never stands, steps or leans toward the camera and never yawns or shows its teeth. No audio.
whyChosen: Home hero: a street dog, left in peace, wakes in its own time and looks up.

title: House sparrow taking a bath
prompt: Start: A male house sparrow (grey crown, chestnut nape and sides of the head, small black bib, warm brown back streaked with black, pale grey-white cheeks and belly) perches on the left rim of a wide, shallow, heavy terracotta bowl of clear, clean water with one small smooth grey stone in it. Three-quarter side view, facing right, looking down at the water with bright interest, beak closed, feathers sleek. The bowl is low and wide, about 70% of the frame width, centred, seen from slightly above so the water surface shows as a bright oval: clear water over the warm clay, with a soft white highlight and no blue, green or teal tint. The bowl's base rests on an implied level ground line at about 82% of the frame height. The sparrow is about 32% of the frame height tall. At least 12% empty margin on every side; nothing else in the frame. End: Edit of the input image. Keep the same house sparrow, the same wide shallow terracotta bowl of clear water with its small grey stone, the same camera angle, framing, scale and colours, and the same perfectly flat pure green (#00FF00) background exactly. Change only the sparrow: it has hopped down into the shallow water and stands in the middle of the bowl, happily bathing, its feathers fluffed up, its wings half-open and shaking, with a few small, bright, clear water droplets in the air around it. Its eye is bright and its beak is closed. The sparrow stays fully inside the frame with at least 12% margin on every side. Nothing else changes: no new objects, no food, no text, no people or hands, no green, teal or turquoise on the bird, bowl or water. Keep the background flat pure green; do not make it transparent. Motion: Locked-off static shot, the camera never moves. The house sparrow perched on the rim of the shallow terracotta water bowl hops down into the clear water, dips its head and splashes happily, fluttering its wings in a little bath so small bright droplets sparkle around it, then stands in the water with its feathers fluffed up. The bowl, the stone and the flat pure green background stay perfectly still. Gentle, cheerful, natural bird movement. No people, no text.
whyChosen: Awareness page, kindness section: instead of bread, a shallow bowl of water, and the bath it brings.

title: Ten neighbours on one street
alt: AI illustration: a sunny Indian street where ten animal neighbours sit in their usual spots: a black kite on a roof corner, a pigeon on a balcony railing, a dog at a gate, a cat on a wall, a palm squirrel in a flowering tree, a crow on a window grill, a myna on a rooftop ledge, a sparrow on a tiled roof, a cow resting by a shop shutter and a koel in a fig tree.
prompt: A wide, sunny Indian residential street seen straight on from across the road at first-floor height, like a stage set: a row of low buildings, two trees and a quiet, clean pavement, with open pale sky above and no one about. All ten animal neighbours from the model sheet are present, each in its usual perch. Each is separated from the others by open space and drawn a little larger than real scale, so even the sparrow is easy to spot. From left to right: (1) Far left, the tallest building, a three-storey cream apartment block. A black kite (the brown bird of prey with a hooked yellow beak) perches on the top corner of its roof parapet, and a rock pigeon sits on the railing of its second-floor balcony. At street level, the fawn Indie dog sits calmly just outside the block's open iron gate, with a small white rice-flour kolam on the step. (2) Left of centre, a low compound wall of cream plaster with a terracotta coping, with the orange-and-white street cat sitting on top. Behind it, a flame-of-the-forest tree in bloom with clusters of bright orange flowers, where a three-striped palm squirrel sits upright on a branch. (3) Centre, a two-storey pale-turquoise house. A house crow perches on the outer bar of a flat, decorative iron grill fixed over a first-floor window. On its flat roof, a common myna stands on the parapet ledge beside a wide terracotta bowl of clean water. (4) Right of centre, a single-storey house with a sloping red clay-tiled roof. A house sparrow stands on the roof's lower edge with a wisp of dry grass in its beak for its nest. (5) Far right, a small corner shop with its rolling shutter pulled down under a plain striped awning, and a closed green waste bin with its lid shut beside it. The cream zebu cow, with its hump and small brass bell, lies resting on the pavement in front of the shutter, legs folded, calm. A large fig tree heavy with ripe red figs leans over the shop, and a glossy black male Asian koel with a red eye sits among its leaves. (Then re-rendered with hand-inked outlines. We also asked for the crow’s, sparrow’s and squirrel’s markings to be corrected; they are still not quite right.)
whyChosen: Awareness page, ‘Spot the neighbour’: every animal in its usual spot, each a link to its card.
